newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland picks JP Morgan to lead manage dollar bond.
newsitem.headline: Poland picks JP Morgan to lead manage dollar bond.

text.p: Poland appointed JP Morgan to manage its planned dollar-denominated international bond issue in 1997, the Finance Ministry said in a statement on Friday.
"After a detailed review of final offers the (selection) commission decided to entrust JP Morgan bank with the task of preparing the issue and leading the issue consortium," the ministry said.
The ministry statement did not give details such as timing or size, and ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.

Poland previously said it planned either a yankee bond or a samurai bond or both this year to establish its presence in other markets after succesful issues of dollar and mark eurobonds in 1995 and 1996.
Ministry officials have said the first issue was planned for mid-year, possibly in July.
The government is authorised to issue up to $500 million worth of international bonds this year.
The statement said six investment banks were invited to bid for the lead manager role apart from JP Morgan.

The ministry said the commission took into account the bidders' experience in arranging similar issues, proposed pricing, costs, placement strategy, the make-up of the offering team and the scope of their past cooperation with Poland. @
JP Morgan led Poland's $250 million eurobond in 1995 when the country returned to international financial markets after clinching a crucial debt restructuring deal with its commercial bank creditors.
Poland's sovereign debt now has a BBB-minus Standard & Poor's rating, a Baa3 from Moody's and BBB from IBCA.
